name: Rivoli
summary: 14 January 1797, and the hardest ground the design has to hold up on. Alvinczi comes down off Monte Baldo in separate columns divided by torrent gullies that let no one lane see the next, Quasdanovich marches up the Adige road under the cliffs with the guns and the horse, and Lusignan is already round the bottom of the plateau and behind the French. Bonaparte has four thousand fewer men and one advantage: he is standing in the middle of all of it, and they arrive one at a time. The Field is a reading of the plateau above Rivoli Veronese rather than a survey of it: the slope down from the north, the river trench cut a hundred metres deep along the east, and one road up out of the gorge past the chapel of San Marco.

armies.name: French
armies.brief: Hold the plateau until Rey's column comes up from Castelnuovo. They outnumber you and they cannot help each other: three lanes off the heights that only meet where you are standing, and a fourth coming up the gorge one man wide past the chapel. Beat them as they arrive, and keep something in hand for the one that walks on behind you.

armies.name: Austrian
armies.brief: Six columns on one plateau, and the ground has already decided that they arrive separately. The gullies part your line until it is down on the flat, the Adige road is a defile a battalion has to file up, and Lusignan is behind them and alone until you reach him. Come down together or be beaten in detail. The chapel is the gate, and Rivoli is what the day is counted on.

chapters.title: Six columns, one plateau
chapters.text: 14 January 1797. Alvinczi has brought the last Austrian army in Italy down off Monte Baldo to break the siege of Mantua, and it is arriving on the Rivoli plateau in separate columns divided by torrent gullies that keep them from seeing one another. Bonaparte has four thousand fewer men and one advantage: he is standing in the middle of all of it. Watch the north edge — they come one at a time, which is the only reason this is a battle.

chapters.title: Quasdanovich comes up the Adige road
chapters.text: IR 10 walks on at the top right, off the road running under the cliffs from the Adige. To reach the plateau it has to file up the defile past the chapel of San Marco a battalion at a time — the gorge is a Crossing here for the same reason a bridge is, because only a column fits through it. Everything Quasdanovich has will arrive in the order that gap allows.

chapters.title: The batteries are laid on each other
chapters.text: Eight Austrian guns on the slope above the plateau, seven French run out two hundred metres in front of them. A battery reaches most of a kilometre here and every battalion on the plateau stands inside that, so this is the one fight on the Field whose loser pays for it in somebody else's ranks. Bonaparte sites his guns to answer Alvinczi's rather than to sweep the ground the columns are coming down.

chapters.title: Lusignan is behind them
chapters.text: Lusignan's battalion walks on at the western edge, in the French rear. It is the manoeuvre that was meant to finish Bonaparte and instead finished Lusignan: he is behind an army that still has somewhere to fall back to, and he is alone until the rest of Alvinczi reaches him.

chapters.title: Rey comes up from Castelnuovo
chapters.text: The head of Rey's column arrives from the south, onto the same ground Lusignan is standing on. Lusignan is now between the French line and the French reserve, which is the position he spent the morning marching into.

chapters.title: The gorge gives up its horse and guns
chapters.text: Quasdanovich's horse battery breaks beside the chapel and his dragoons follow inside the minute. Everything he has came up the defile a battalion at a time and formed on the lip of it with nothing behind, so it is beaten in the order the gap let it out — which is what a Crossing costs an army that has to attack through one.

chapters.title: San Marco changes hands
chapters.text: The chapel goes Austrian, and is French again a quarter of a minute later. IR 10 gets onto the ground with the last of the Adige column and is thrown straight back off it, and then it breaks. This is the point at which the day could have gone the other way: hold the chapel and the rest of the column walks up behind him.

chapters.title: Belgiojoso breaks in the centre
chapters.text: IR 44 breaks. The columns coming down off the heights reach the flat one at a time and each is met by a line that is already formed and already facing it. That is the arithmetic Alvinczi's plan never got round, and it is the same arithmetic all afternoon.

chapters.title: The French guns are broken where they stand
chapters.text: Bonaparte loses his battery to the duel he sited it for. It is the bill and not the failure: Positionsbatterie Nr. 4 spent the morning firing at guns instead of at the line on the plateau, and the battalions that would otherwise have paid for that are still standing in it.

chapters.title: Joubert's centre gives
chapters.text: The 33e breaks, the first French battalion of the day to go. It has held the ground between the gullies since the first column came down them, and there is nothing Austrian left on that side to come through the gap it leaves — the centre was spent breaking it.

chapters.title: Lusignan is finished
chapters.text: Lusignan's battalion breaks in the French rear and his grenadiers go three minutes behind it. In the event most of that command was taken prisoner: the column sent to cut Bonaparte's retreat found it had none of its own.

chapters.title: The last push on the plateau
chapters.text: IR 48 breaks trying to come onto Rivoli itself. It is the last thing Alvinczi has that is still going forward. The firing does not stop with it — Masséna's two regiments both break in the last five minutes and neither leaves the Field — but there is nothing Austrian left to walk into the ground they give.

chapters.title: What it was worth
chapters.text: Rivoli ended the fourth and last Austrian attempt to relieve Mantua. The city surrendered a fortnight later, and northern Italy went with it.
